messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: realtime detector triggered — elevated latencies for route /v1/generate in us-east-1 (5m window). 95th=450ms (SLO=300ms), 99th=1.8s (SLO=1.0s). Streaming stalls up ~3.4x, KV-cache miss rate jumped 4% -> 42%. Dashboard: https://redwood-infra.internal/d/latency/realtime?orgId=1&var-region=us-east-1

maria: oncall here — seeing the alert. paging now and starting quick triage. @alex can you +1 if you have bandwidth? :eyes:

alex: I'm available, joining. pulling dashboards now.

priya: adding context — we just rolled out kv-cache v2.1 to ~40% of us-east-1 yesterday (canary). Could be related.

sam: quick checks: tailing stream logs shows repeated stalls with message "kv-cache-miss spike" and backlog growth in the batching queue. small number of OOMs in the runtime (1-2 pods) but not widespread.

maria: ok plan for initial triage: 1) confirm scope (pct of traffic impacted) 2) check canary vs non-canary diff 3) attempt fast mitigation (route around canary or enable fallback variant) 4) escalate/paging if customer-impact > 1%

kyle: scope quick look — over last 5m ~0.9% of total requests are experiencing >1s tail latency, but streaming sessions show higher error ratio (~2.6% failed frames). Most affected in us-east-1 / stream-model pool.

maria: sounds like limited customer impact but breaching p99 SLOs. marking incident severity: Sev 2 for now. paging oncall roster and alerting SRE. @ops-bot please create incident ticket and page SREs.

ops-bot: Created INC-2026-4578. Paged oncall SREs: @sam, @kyle. Link: https://redwood-infra.internal/incidents/INC-2026-4578

alex: checking canary diff — metrics by deployment tag: canary hosts p99=2.2s, stable hosts p99=0.9s. Kv-cache miss rate by tag: canary 48% vs stable 3%. strong signal pointing at kv-cache rollout.

priya: fwiw the kv-cache v2.1 rollout included a small change to TTL and prefetch behavior. Prefetch disabled for streaming clients by mistake in canary (bad flag).

maria: direct mitigation options: A) rollback kv-cache v2.1 from canary hosts B) re-enable prefetch flag C) route streaming traffic off canary using smart-routing policy D) enable fallback lightweight model for streaming to reduce mem pressure. Which is fastest?

sam: fastest is C (route off canary) + B (re-enable prefetch) if we can push config toggle. rollback (A) is heavier and takes longer to confirm. D reduces quality but buys time if mem pressure persists.

maria: doing step C now — updating routing policy to deprioritize canary tag for stream endpoints in us-east-1. Command:```
# routing toggle
redwoodctl routing set-priority --region us-east-1 --route /v1/generate --avoid-tag kv-cache-v2.1
```

alex: saw route change apply, trafffic shifting ~70% off canary within 60s. p99 on aggregate dropping to ~1.1s. good signal.

kyle: concurrently toggling prefetch flag on canary hosts (if we can):```
# toggle prefetch
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/kv-cache PREFETCH_ENABLED=true --context=canary-us-east-1
```

sam: logs show prefetch flag applied on 6 canary pods. observing immediate decrease in miss rate — canary miss rate now 18% (was 48%).

maria: marked mitigation progress: routing step + prefetch toggle. overall p99 now ~850ms and p95 ~290ms. still above SLO for p99 (1.0s) but trending down. continuing watch.

priya: root cause summary candidate: misconfigured prefetch toggle in kv-cache v2.1 rollout causing high miss rates and increased backend load -> streaming stalls and queue backlog -> p95/p99 regression.

maria: customers impacted: small set of streaming sessions — we have 3 customers reporting degraded streaming freshness, no full outages. posting customer-facing status note in support channel.

alex: ops-bot reports autoscale activity: "autoscaler scaled pool-stream-1 from 12 -> 18 nodes 2m ago" — that helped throughput but didn't address root cause.

ops-bot: Autoscale events logged: 2026-03-15T18:04:12Z pool-stream-1 scaled +6 (policy=load).

maria: decision: keep routing still avoiding canary for another 30m, continue monitoring, prepare rollback plan for kv-cache v2.1 if miss rate doesn't fully normalize. Sam will own the rollback playbook if needed; Priya to coordinate release team.

sam: acknowledged, prepped rollback steps (will require drain and restart of canary hosts, ~8-12m downtime for canary fraction).

kyle: logging note: I'll collect a 10m packet of stream traces and attach to INC-2026-4578 for postmortem.

maria: handing a short oncall update to @alex in 25m — I need to jump to a customer call. Alex please maintain watch and escalate if p99 > 1.2s or errors > 3%.

alex: taking the handoff. I'll be on watch and will page if thresholds breach.

priya: adding retrospective action items: - add automated canary sanity check for kv-cache prefetch flag - tighter rollout gating for stateful cache changes - dashboard alert for kv-cache miss rate > 10%

maria: thanks team. leaving a quick summary for the incident ticket. Will follow up with timeline and postmortem owner after stable. :thumbsup:

alex: noted. keeping channel open for 30m watch then will archive. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-4578 updated: severity=SEV2, status=mitigated (monitoring). Updated at 6765432165."
